In sqlparse/sql.py, IdentifierList.get_identifiers() had an inverted condition: it was yielding whitespace and comma punctuation tokens while skipping actual identifier tokens, contradicting its own docstring ("Whitespaces and punctuations are not included in this generator"). This broke _process_identifierlist in sqlparse/filters/aligned_indent.py, which relies on get_identifiers() to correctly align SELECT column lists etc. when reindent_aligned=True, causing the 24 reported 'format reindent aligned' regressions.

Fix applied:
```python
for token in self.tokens:
    if not (token.is_whitespace or token.match(T.Punctuation, ',')):
        yield token
```

Verified manually that sqlparse.format(..., reindent_aligned=True) now produces correctly aligned output for a basic SELECT/FROM/WHERE/AND query, matching expected formatting conventions (column list aligned under SELECT, keywords right-aligned).
